jobs.title: ICMS Case Manager
jobs.description:
Scope Of Responsibility

The ICMS Case Manager works within a multi-disciplinary field-based team of clinicians, case managers, employment specialists and community partners to assist in the development, implementation and monitoring of a service/treatment plan for residents living at the Nest on Florence , a 51-unit housing development and/or scattered site apartment sites in the South Los Angeles area offering permanent housing to the Transition Age Youth Population ages 18-25.

The ICMS Case Manager practices with a healing centered, trauma informed approach that focuses on harm reduction and housing first to offer quality support to young people. In addition, the ICMS Case Manager balances accountability with life skill building so that young people can sustain and maintain their housing.

Essential Functions

Formulates individualized service plans that identify the young person’s personal, social, emotional, mental health, educational, medical, housing, physical and/or financial needs and goals in collaboration with the ICMS program participants.
Mediates and advocates on behalf of clients to help them obtain and keep suitable housing, health care, jobs and mental health services, education/school services, benefit entitlements, etc.
Searches the community and presents options for additional needed or desired services (e.g. emancipation services; sober living opportunities; education enrichment; scholarships, grants or job training programs; age-appropriate social opportunities; parenting classes).
Connects to resources such as health insurance, housing, low-cost childcare, chemical dependency, education, mental health, medical care, housing, income (SSI, GR) and employment, depending on specific service needs. Provides linkage to participants to health, mental health, and substance use services as needed and assist participants in maintaining treatment regimens.
Collaborates with participants (and other service providers) to maintain housing stability goals.
Works with Property Management to Assist participants in lease signing, adhering to the lease requirements and understanding tenant rights and responsibilities.
Provides field-based support to young people including transporting them to resources and appointments, empowering them to access different layers of support.
Provides outreach, housing navigation and housing location services.
Attends and participates in Care Coordination Meetings for SA 6 and various other community meetings, and documents services in multiple electronic online databases (Exym, HMIS, CHAMP).
Attends case conference meetings to assist and participate in case disposition and follow-up.
Provides interagency and intra-agency consultation, communication, coordination and referrals.
Completes and submits progress notes in a 24-hour timeframe utilizing the agency’s electronic health record system (EXYM, Clarity/HMIS, CHAMP) and collaborative documentation while serving clients; discusses and receives proof of insurance / Medi-Cal information in the field and submits to the QMET and/or IS Support Team.
Maintains a caseload of 20 participants and sees them one time per week at minimum.
Meets agency’s productivity standards for client service hours, if applicable.
Represents Wellnest at community resource events as needed.
Provides 24 hour on call care to residents of the Nest on Florence, and after care support to previous residents as needed.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field, with an emphasis in community mental health work.
One year of experience working with homeless individuals, OR a minimum of two years of experience providing direct mental health or intensive case management services, unless otherwise approved by DHS.
Experience working with clients with mental illness, chronic health issues, and substance use disorders.
Have expertise in the following areas: chronic homelessness, outreach and engagement strategies, intensive case management services, best practice models, mental health and substance use disorder services, crisis intervention, suicide assessment and prevention, affordable housing and public benefits applications, housing and landlord/tenant rights, eviction prevention, etc.

Certificates, Licenses And Registrations

Must possess and maintain a valid CA driver’s license and insurable driving record.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

A strong commitment to advancing Wellnest’s mission.
Ability to utilize a healing-centered, harm reduction, and housing first approach.
Ability to conduct initial and quarterly psychosocial assessments with participants referred by the Department of Health Services (DHS).
Knowledge of surrounding poverty, homelessness, substance use, and social factors related to each dynamic, preferred.
Knowledge about services for homeless individuals and families throughout Los Angeles County.
Knowledge of challenges associated with homelessness, including chemical dependency, mental disorders, physical health concerns, violence, and isolation.
Ability to understand the needs of homeless young people to develop collaborative goals towards greater self-sufficiency and independence in the larger community.
Ability to work a flexible schedule, including some evenings and weekends.

Conditions Of Employment

Employee may be asked to pursue additional training when it is determined to be in the best interest of the company. Employee must have the ability to use a personal vehicle with the required insurance coverage to complete the essential duties of their job and conduct agency business. Employee must maintain a valid California driver’s license and clean driving record that meets Wellnest’s insurance carrier’s criteria for liability coverage. In keeping with Company policy for all employees, the successful applicant must also complete a test for TB, and fingerprint clearance by the Department of Justice. Employee must agree to Wellnest's Arbitration Agreement as a condition of employment.

Working Conditions

Employee regularly works out in the field and in an office environment. Employee may be required to work flexible, evening and/or weekend hours for time-sensitive projects.

Reasoning Ability

Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions
Ability to read, analyze and interpret manual and office documents
Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.
Ability to define problems, gather, transcribe and post data, analyze, synthesize and classify information, and draw valid conclusions.
Ability to work independently and with others - including other employees, clients and members of the public - in face-to-face and telephonic contexts.
Ability to multi-task, establish priorities and manage time, meet deadlines and perform duties under time constraints.
Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work demands.
Maintain a high level of concentration and attention to detail for extended periods of time.
Maintain a high level of ethical and professional standards in accordance with agency policy.

Physical Demands

Ability to talk or hear in order to give and receive information and instructions.
Ability to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls
Ability to reach with hands and arms.
Ability to use computer keyboard up to 50% of the day.
Visual acuity, ability to adjust focus and peripheral vision for work on a laptop or other computer equipment.
Lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
Able to use telephone, office copier, calculator, fax machine, computer printer and scanner, or other equipment as required.

Description

Job Summary:

This position serves as a lead-level resource for assigned programs by providing operational support, assisting with staff oversight, monitoring program performance, and ensuring high-quality Enhanced Care Management (ECM) services are delivered in accordance with organizational, contractual, and regulatory requirements

Essential Functions

Program Operations and Leadership

Oversee and support the day-to-day operations of assigned programs, ensuring services are delivered effectively and in alignment with program goals, grant requirements, contractual obligations, and EPU standards.
Assist with the supervision, training, coaching, and mentoring of assigned staff to promote quality service delivery and professional development.
Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned programs and represent the department in the absence of the Manager or Director, as designated.
Coordinate staffing and service delivery schedules to ensure continuity of services during staff absences, vacancies, and changing program needs.
Monitor program operations and service quality to ensure compliance with organizational policies, funding requirements, and applicable regulations.
Collect, track, analyze, summarize, and report program data, outcomes, and performance measures required by funding sources, organizational leadership, and program objectives.
Ensure assigned staff conduct required home visits and maintain regular contact with families as outlined in care plans, program standards, and contractual requirements.
Assist in identifying operational challenges and implementing solutions to improve program efficiency, effectiveness, and participant outcomes.

Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Service Delivery

Maintain and manage an assigned ECM caseload, as needed, ensuring timely and effective service delivery.
Engage eligible members and coordinate services with individuals, providers, agencies, and community partners to ensure a seamless member experience and avoid duplication of services.
Support the Supervisor in overseeing the delivery of ECM services and implementation of individualized care plans.
Deliver services in locations most accessible and appropriate for members, including where they live, seek care, or otherwise receive services, in accordance with health plan requirements.
Connect members to community resources, social services, transportation, and community supports that address identified needs.
Advocate on behalf of members with healthcare providers and other service systems to improve access to care and resources.
Coordinate with hospitals, healthcare providers, and community partners regarding discharge planning, treatment adherence, medication management, and continuity of care.

Accompany members to appointments, when appropriate and permitted under health plan guidelines.
Provide health education, health promotion, self-management support, and coaching to assist members in achieving their health and wellness goals.

Ability to follow detailed procedures, prioritize competing tasks, and complete documentation accurately and on time.

EPU facility hours are Monday – Friday; 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM; with some exceptions based on business needs. Positions hours may vary depending upon the needs of the business.
Perform other duties as they are assigned by the Sr. Manager, Program Director, and/or President/Chief Executive Officer.

Requirements

Knowledge and Skills

Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, able to make independent decisions when handling sensitive family and child information, within guidelines. Strong problem-solving, critical thinking, and decision-making skills.

Experience

2+ years of experience providing direct services to children, families, or vulnerable populations.
2+ years of experience working with families impacted by, or at risk for, abuse, neglect, trauma, or other significant social challenges.
2+ years of case management or care coordination experience, including connecting individuals and families to community resources and support services.
1+ years’ experience in case management principles, care coordination practices, family support services, and community resources
1+ years of experience in a supervisory, lead worker, or staff oversight experience.
1+ years of experience working with diverse populations and demonstrating cultural responsiveness when providing services.
1+ years of experience engaging families in problem-solving, advocacy, resource coordination, and goal achievement.

Bilingual in English and Spanish or English and Hmong.
Experience working in Enhanced Care Management (ECM), CalAIM, Medi-Cal Managed Care, social services, behavioral health, or related health and human services programs.
Experience using Apricot or other electronic case management or data-tracking systems.
Must be computer literate with experience in maintaining accurate records, entering data, and documenting services within an electronic database or case management system. Working with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams.

Licenses And Other Requirements

Possess a good driving record with no serious violation for the past three-year period and be able to provide proof of current automobile liability insurance that meets the minimum standard that meets the State of California requirements. Reliable transportation and the ability to travel throughout the service area to conduct home visits, attend meetings, and provide community-based services.

About The Role

The Care Coordinator is the day-to-day link between clients, Caregivers, staffing, recruiting, and HR.
The primary focus is keeping client schedules fully staffed, communicating changes quickly, and solving problems before they affect service. This role also supports recruiting, hiring, onboarding, orientation, employee relations, and basic HR documentation for Caregivers. Success requires strong follow-through, good judgment, comfort with difficult conversations, and the ability to shift priorities in a fast-paced home care environment.

What Success Looks Like

95%+ staffing rate with open shifts addressed quickly and accurately.
Client turnover maintained below 3.5% through responsive service and proactive follow-up.
90%+ client and caregiver satisfaction through clear communication and dependable support.
New Caregivers move through hiring, onboarding, and orientation promptly and with complete documentation.
Employee issues, attendance concerns, and policy violations are documented and addressed consistently.

What You'll Do

Keep client schedules fully staffed by matching Caregivers to client needs, covering open shifts, resolving call-outs, and communicating changes quickly.
Support clients, families, and Caregivers by responding to concerns, solving service issues, documenting activity, and following through until problems are resolved.

Comfort handling high-volume phone, text, and email communication with clients, applicants, and employees.
Ability to have clear, respectful conversations about attendance, performance, policy expectations, and corrective action.

Scope Of Responsibility

The ICMS Case Manager works within a multi-disciplinary field-based team of clinicians, case managers, employment specialists and community partners to assist in the development, implementation and monitoring of a service/treatment plan for residents living at the Nest on Florence , a 51-unit housing development and/or scattered site apartment sites in the South Los Angeles area offering permanent housing to the Transition Age Youth Population ages 18-25.

In addition, the ICMS Case Manager balances accountability with life skill building so that young people can sustain and maintain their housing.

Essential Functions

Formulates individualized service plans that identify the young person’s personal, social, emotional, mental health, educational, medical, housing, physical and/or financial needs and goals in collaboration with the ICMS program participants.
Mediates and advocates on behalf of clients to help them obtain and keep suitable housing, health care, jobs and mental health services, education/school services, benefit entitlements, etc.
Searches the community and presents options for additional needed or desired services (e.g. emancipation services; sober living opportunities; education enrichment; scholarships, grants or job training programs; age-appropriate social opportunities; parenting classes).
Connects to resources such as health insurance, housing, low-cost childcare, chemical dependency, education, mental health, medical care, housing, income (SSI, GR) and employment, depending on specific service needs. Provides linkage to participants to health, mental health, and substance use services as needed and assist participants in maintaining treatment regimens.
Collaborates with participants (and other service providers) to maintain housing stability goals.
Works with Property Management to Assist participants in lease signing, adhering to the lease requirements and understanding tenant rights and responsibilities.
Provides field-based support to young people including transporting them to resources and appointments, empowering them to access different layers of support.
Provides outreach, housing navigation and housing location services.
Attends and participates in Care Coordination Meetings for SA 6 and various other community meetings, and documents services in multiple electronic online databases (Exym, HMIS, CHAMP).
Attends case conference meetings to assist and participate in case disposition and follow-up.

We recognize that a person’s life experiences can provide firsthand knowledge relevant to being successful in the work that we do.

To recognize and meet the distinctive needs of youth ages 18-24 who are experiencing homelessness by providing stable housing, mental health care, case management, life skills training, and connection to community services and resources with the ultimate goal of assisting all clients in obtaining and sustaining safe and stable housing.

Use agency vehicles to provide client transportation and support youth with appointments, housing-related activities, and other approved service needs.
Maintain current knowledge of community resources and develop effective working relationships with internal programs, housing providers, and community partners.
Attend required supervision, staff meetings, trainings, clinical meetings, and other meetings as assigned.
Maintain regular and reliable attendance and an on-site presence consistent with shelter operations and the needs of youth being served.
Participate in program quality improvement, data collection, special projects, and other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Secondary Duties

Work effectively, respectfully, and ethically with a diverse group of clients, co-workers, volunteers, partners, and members of the public.
Comply with the Volunteers of America, Utah Code of Ethics and all agency policies and procedures.
Use sound judgment and seek supervision or additional support when situations exceed the scope of the position or require management involvement.

Position Overview

The Business Analytics team is seeking a Data Analyst with strong business acumen and SQL skills to deliver high-impact insights and build scalable solutions. This role blends technical execution (data development, automation, dashboards) with financial and commercial goals (financial analysis, interpreting results, supporting data driven decision-making). The ideal candidate is a self-starter who is comfortable operating independently, partnering directly with business stakeholders, and taking ownership of analytical solutions from development through deployment.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnership

Partner with Finance and other stakeholders to turn vaguely-formed ideas into business questions with clear goals, deliverables, and success metrics.
Identify trends, risks, and opportunities through data analysis.
Develop dashboards within Power BI and present findings and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.

Data & Analytics Development

Design, build, and maintain scalable data models, reporting layers, and analytical solutions using SQL and dbt.
Develop and deploy production-ready code through Git-based workflows and standard CI/CD processes.
Independently troubleshoot data issues, improve data quality, and resolve discrepancies across source systems, transformations, and reporting layers.
Write clean, maintainable, well-documented code and maintain documentation for datasets, business definitions, and transformation logic.

Qualifications (Required)

5–7 years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, analytics engineering, finance analytics, or a related role.
Advanced SQL expertise and strong analytical problem-solving skills.
Experience with dbt and Git version control, including contributing production-ready code through standard development workflows.
Demonstrated ability to independently research, troubleshoot, and implement technical solutions with minimal day-to-day technical oversight.
Logical, analytical thinker with strong finance and business acumen (comfort with KPIs, P&L concepts, budgeting/forecasting, and business performance drivers).
Experience creating dashboards (preferably Power BI) and communicating insights to non-technical audiences.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

Experience supporting FP&A, commercial, revenue operations, or professional services analytics.
Experience working in small or growing analytics teams with end-to-end ownership of analytical solutions.
Ability to apply an 80/20 mindset to prioritize high-impact, pragmatic solutions.
Experience using Python for automation and analytical workflows.
